module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 71

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/71](https://www.erdosproblems.com/71)
- [Bo77] Bollobás, Béla, *Cycles modulo $k$*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1977), 97-98.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Discrete Math. (1997), 227-231.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos71

/--
Is it true that for every infinite arithmetic progression $P$ which contains even numbers
there is some constant $c=c(P)$ such that every graph with average degree at least $c$
contains a cycle whose length is in $P$?

In [Er82e] Erdős credits this conjecture to himself and Burr. This has been proved by
Bollobás [Bo77]. The best dependence of the constant $c(P)$ is unknown.

The infinite arithmetic progression is encoded as a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ satisfying
`P.IsAPOfLength ⊤` (which forces a positive common difference), and "contains even numbers"
as the existence of an even element. The average degree of a finite simple graph is
`SimpleGraph.averageDegree`, i.e. $(\sum_v \deg v)/|V| \in \mathbb{Q}$, and a cycle whose
length is in $P$ is a cycle walk `w` with `w.length ∈ P`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/110d489ed5c07e5b216453e092e9113127c98c9a/problems/71/Erdos71.lean"]
theorem erdos_71 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ P : Set ℕ, P.IsAPOfLength ⊤ → (∃ n ∈ P, Even n) →
      ∃ c : ℚ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
        [DecidableRel G.Adj], c ≤ G.averageDegree →
          ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length ∈ P := by
  sorry

end Erdos71

reformulations.difference: The threshold is explicitly rational (`∃ c : ℚ`), whereas the source asks for an unspecified constant, conventionally allowing a real threshold.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A rational threshold is also a real threshold. Conversely, given a real threshold c, choose a rational q > c. Any graph with average degree at least q also has average degree at least c. The threshold-quantifier equivalence, with the full graph and cycle conditions, was proved in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved (1982), part III, §5, p. 71: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf
https://www.ime.usp.br/~resenhas/ and https://www.ime.usp.br/~resenhas/home/ (journal archive; Er95 full text was unavailable)

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/AP/Basic.lean; FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Degrees.lean; Mathlib's SimpleGraph Basic, Finite, Paths, and Walk/Basic; SetTheory/Cardinal/Finite; Data/Set/Card; Algebra/Group/Even; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean
review.notes:
The sole theorem faithfully states the source's affirmative problem. Lean experiments established that `P.IsAPOfLength ⊤` is equivalent to P = {a + nd : n ∈ ℕ} with d > 0, and that one even term implies arbitrarily large even terms. Empty and singleton progressions are excluded. Checked empty/small graphs, rational average degree (including a computed value 4/3), and the exclusion of cycles shorter than three. Complete graphs show the degree hypothesis cannot be made globally vacuous by choosing a large finite threshold.

The exact linked proof was independently compiled in /workspace/review using its pinned Lean 4.28.0 and Mathlib commit. It matches the repository statement and reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The solved tag and positive answer agree with the source and current status database.

Access limitation: the live problem page returned Cloudflare challenges, so its complete statement and remarks were read through the January 13, 2026 archive. Er82e was read directly; full texts of Bo77, Er95, and Er97b could not be retrieved. These limitations did not prevent comparison with the explicitly stated main source. All experiments were outside the checkout; the reviewed file is unchanged.
